articles.headlineTranslated: Measles infection confirmed in Matsuyama City for the first time in 14 years; two-dose vaccination prevents about 90% of infections and severe illness; vaccination status check [Ehime] (October 13, 2026) | Nankai Broadcasting News NNN
articles.summary: Measles infection confirmed in Matsuyama City, Ehime Prefecture, for the first time in 14 years. A man in his 30s contracted measles; exposure occurred in public places from Oct 1–6, with the case announced by Matsuyama City on Oct 13, 2026. Measles is highly contagious and spreads via airborne transmission; initial symptoms resemble a cold, followed by fever above 39°C and rash. Two-dose vaccination provides about 90% protection against infection and severe illness. Those born before April 2, 1990 may have received only one dose or none due to historical schedules. Experts urge completing two-dose vaccination and checking immunization records (母子手帳) at local clinics. The measles incubation is roughly three weeks, so vigilance should extend for weeks after exposure; there is no specific antiviral treatment, underscoring vaccination as prevention.

articles.headlineTranslated: Measles case confirmed in Matsuyama City for the first time in 14 years; 'the infectivity is extremely strong'; visited supermarkets and drugstores (published October 10, 2026) | Nankai Broadcasting News NNN
articles.summary: Measles case confirmed in Matsuyama City for the first time since 2012. A man in his 30s residing in Matsuyama City tested positive on Oct 10, 2026, after a notification on Oct 9; laboratory confirmation followed. He developed fever, rash, and cough, and had traveled overseas in late September to a region with measles transmission. He has one dose of measles vaccine. Epidemiological investigation found he visited supermarkets and a drugstore in the Matsumatsu area of Matsuyama City on the evenings of Oct 1 and Oct 4–6, potentially exposing many people; no public transport use. The Matsuyama City Health Center is conducting the outbreak response and urges anyone with suspected measles symptoms to contact a medical facility in advance and follow instructions. This marks the first locally confirmed measles infection in Matsuyama since 2012.

articles.headlineTranslated: Measles infection confirmed; in Matsuyama City since 2012; appeal to customers of commercial facilities to take precautions, Ehime.
articles.summary: Measles infection confirmed in Matsuyama City, Ehime Prefecture, Japan. A man in his 30s developed fever and rash on Oct 1 and was laboratory-confirmed on Oct 10, marking the first local measles case since 2012 (14 years). He had traveled to a country designated as a measles infection-expansion area in late September. The patient had one measles vaccination dose. Between Oct 1–6, he visited several supermarkets and drugstores in Matsuyama, potentially contacting many people; no documented transmission to family or workplace, and he did not use public transport. Public health guidance urges those with fever or cough to contact healthcare facilities in advance and avoid public transport when seeking care. Nationwide, measles cases rose from 265 last year to 576 as of Sept 27 this year, highlighting ongoing outbreaks.

articles.headlineTranslated: Warning issued by prefecture over measles; multiple infections reported in Fukuoka Prefecture; call to verify vaccination history and other measures (Posted October 6, 2026) | KRY NEWS NNN
articles.summary: Measles infections are being reported in Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan, with authorities urging residents to verify vaccination history and take precautions. Measles causes high fever and rash and can lead to serious complications or death; it is highly contagious and spreads via airborne droplets. In Yamaguchi Prefecture, on September 12, a man in his 20s living in Fukuoka City was confirmed infected under the Yamaguchi Environment and Health Center. For the week ending September 20, nationwide measles cases reached 15, with Fukuoka accounting for 12 (about 80%). The prefecture emphasizes vaccination as the primary preventive measure: check two-dose vaccination status using the Maternal and Child Health Handbook, and if measles is suspected, avoid crowded places. There is no specific antiviral treatment; two-dose vaccination is effective in prevention.

articles.headlineTranslated: Measles: Concern over the spread of infections within the prefecture; calls for vaccination — Fukuoka Medical Association (published September 30, 2026) | FBS NEWS NNN
articles.summary: Measles outbreaks are being confirmed within Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan, prompting warnings from the Fukuoka Medical Association. As of the week ending September 20, nationwide 15 measles cases were confirmed, with 12 in Fukuoka—about 80% of the total. The association attributes much of the spread to increased international travel and returnees. Measles, characterized by fever above 39°C and rash, is highly contagious and spreads through airborne transmission. In a press conference on September 30, the association urged vaccination and other measures. Because simple hygiene like handwashing and masking is insufficient for prevention, individuals with symptoms are advised to contact healthcare providers beforehand and seek care promptly. The association specifically calls for vaccination of children who have not completed the routine immunization schedule.

articles.headlineTranslated: Influenza on the rise; 12 measles cases confirmed in Fukuoka (Published on September 28, 2026) | FBS NEWS NNN
articles.summary: Influenza is in the influenza season in Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan, with weekly reported influenza cases per medical institution rising 1.2-fold to 5.34 in the week ending September 20. The prefecture had already announced the season’s start in early September and urges continued hand hygiene, masking, ventilation, and vigilance to curb transmission. Separately, measles (ha sika) numbers are rising, with 12 laboratory-confirmed measles cases reported in the same week, bringing the season total to 22 in Fukuoka. Measles symptoms include fever of 39°C or higher and rash. Health officials warn of ongoing spread and reiterate vaccination and pre-screening. Those with suspected measles should contact healthcare facilities before visiting and avoid using public transport when seeking care.

articles.headlineTranslated: [Measles] Four cases confirmed; total of 10 cases in Fukuoka Prefecture this year (Published September 14, 2026) | FBS NEWS NNN
articles.summary: Measles outbreaks in Fukuoka Prefecture reach 10 cases this year as of September 14, 2026, with four new infections reported. A woman in her 20s residing in Fukuoka City developed fever, fatigue, sore throat, and rash; genetic testing on September 13 confirmed measles. She had two prior vaccine doses and no overseas travel history. An additional three infections were announced in Fukuoka City and Kurume City, bringing the annual total to 10. Public health authorities emphasize vaccination as a preventive measure, noting that handwashing or masking alone cannot fully prevent spread, and advise individuals with suspected measles symptoms to contact a medical facility and avoid using public transport when seeking care to reduce transmission.

articles.headlineTranslated: First measles case of the year in Yamaguchi Prefecture; a man in his 20s from Fukuoka Prefecture came to the prefecture by Shinkansen.
articles.summary: Measles diagnosed in Yamaguchi Prefecture, Japan—the first measles case in the prefecture in 2026. A man in his 20s from Fukuoka City visited Yamaguchi and traveled there by Shinkansen Nozomi 14 (car 1, non-reserved). He developed fever on Sept 9; rash appeared on Sept 12. He disembarked at Shin-Yamaguchi around 9:10 am and sought medical care the same day. PCR testing at the Environmental Health Center confirmed measles. He is currently under medical care in Yamaguchi Prefecture. The case is considered imported to Yamaguchi due to his origin from Fukuoka. Details on exposure, contact tracing, or vaccination status were not provided. Public health authorities have confirmed the case and are monitoring the potential for further spread as of Sept 14, 2026.
